inputs.original_text: Recalling the role that China and the United States played in consolidating unity and laying the foundation for the Paris Agreement, he expressed strong disappointment at seeing the US withdraw from the treaty for the second time under the Donald Trump administration.
inputs.modified_text: It’s understandable that he misses the appearance of US-China unity, but international agreement isn’t an end in itself. A government’s first duty is to its own people, families, and national sovereignty—not to preserve a global treaty simply to satisfy diplomatic expectations. Trump’s withdrawal may disappoint advocates of the Paris Agreement, but standing apart from an international consensus can be a defense of national accountability, not a rejection of responsibility.
